8.1 From notebook to service Many models never reach real users. They work in a notebook, on one laptop. Production asks harder questions. In production, a model must answer requests from many users at once, return results in under a second, survive bad inputs, and keep working when the data changes. It must also be reproducible: you should know which model version, code and data produced any prediction. MLOps (machine learning operations) borrows ideas from software engineering to make this routine. Notebook Production service "It worked yesterday" Versioned code, data and models Accuracy on a test set Accuracy, speed, cost and uptime, measured continuously Saving a trained model Save the whole fitted pipeline, preprocessing included, so the service never scales inputs differently from training. Python · save_model.py import joblib from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True) pipe = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)).fit(X, y) joblib.dump(pipe, "model_v1.joblib") # version in the file name loaded = joblib.load("model_v1.joblib") print("same predictions:", (loaded.predict(X[:5]) _= pipe.predict(X[:5])).all()) OUTPUT same predictions: True ✦ KEY IDEA Treat a model like any release: version it, record its data and code, and keep the previous version ready to roll back.

8.2 Building an API with FastAPI An API (application programming interface) lets a website or app send data to your model and get predictions back. FastAPI is a popular Python framework for this. You describe the expected input with a Pydantic model, and FastAPI checks every request against it automatically, rejecting bad data with a clear error. It also builds interactive documentation at /docs . Python · app.py import joblib from fastapi import FastAPI from pydantic import BaseModel, Field app = FastAPI(title="Review sentiment API", version="1.0.0") model = joblib.load("sentiment_v1.joblib") # loaded once, at startup class Review(BaseModel): text: str = Field(min_length=3, max_length=2000) class Prediction(BaseModel): positive: float label: str model_version: str @app.post("/predict", response_model=Prediction) def predict(review: Review): p = float(model.predict_proba([review.text])[0, 1]) return Prediction(positive=round(p, 3), label="positive" if p _= 0.5 else "negative", model_version="1.0.0") Terminal · run and call uvicorn app:app curl -X POST localhost:8000/predict -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"text": "fast delivery and fresh food"}' ✦ KEY IDEA Load the model once at startup, not per request: loading takes seconds, a prediction milliseconds.

8.3 Packaging with Docker "It works on my machine" is the oldest problem in software. A container packages your code, libraries and model into one image that runs the same way everywhere. Think of a shipping container: whatever is inside, every port in the world can load, stack and move it with the same equipment. A Docker image is that container for software. It is built from a Dockerfile , a short recipe listing the base system, the libraries to install and the command to start the app. Dockerfile · Dockerfile FROM python:3.11-slim WORKDIR /app COPY requirements.txt . RUN pip install _-no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY app.py sentiment_v1.joblib ./ EXPOSE 8000 CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "_-host", "0.0.0.0", "_-port", "8000"] Terminal · build and run docker build -t sentiment-api:1.0.0 . docker run -p 8000:8000 sentiment-api:1.0.0 Option What it is Good for Serverless functions Code runs per request; no server to manage Light models, websites, demos Container platforms Run your Docker image as a service Most model APIs GPU servers Machines with graphics cards Large models you host yourself Hosted model APIs Call a provider’s model over HTTP LLMs and embeddings without hardware ▲ SECRETS STAY OUTSIDE THE IMAGE Never copy API keys or passwords into a Docker image or a code repository. Pass them as environment variables when the container starts, through your hosting platform’s settings.

8.4 Deploying with CI/CD Continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) means every change is tested and released automatically, so shipping is boring, fast and safe. 1 Push. You commit code to a Git repository such as GitHub. 2 Test. A CI service runs the tests automatically: code tests, plus a model check that accuracy hasn’t dropped below an agreed level. 3 Release. When the main branch updates, the new version goes live. If something breaks, roll back to the previous version in one click. YAML · .github/workflows/test.yml on: [push, pull_request] jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - run: pip install -r requirements.txt pytest _& pytest -q Python · test_model.py from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer import joblib from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score def test_model_quality(): # pytest runs functions named test_* X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True) pipe = joblib.load("model_v1.joblib") # saved in section 8.1 score = cross_val_score(pipe, X, y, cv=5).mean() assert score > 0.95, f"accuracy dropped to {score:.3f}" return score print(f"cross-validated accuracy: {test_model_quality():.3f} (test passed)") OUTPUT cross-validated accuracy: 0.981 (test passed)

8.5 Monitoring and data drift The world changes after launch. Customers change habits, prices rise, new products appear. A model trained on last year’s data slowly becomes wrong, often without any error message. Data drift means the inputs change: the average order value in production no longer looks like training. Concept drift means the relationship changes: the same inputs now lead to different outcomes, as when a new competitor changes why customers leave. Monitoring compares live data with training data and raises an alert when they diverge. Python · drift.py import numpy as np from scipy.stats import ks_2samp rng = np.random.default_rng(5) train_orders = rng.lognormal(7.5, 0.5, 5000) # order values at training this_week = rng.lognormal(7.8, 0.5, 800) # prices have risen stat, p = ks_2samp(train_orders, this_week) print(f"median then: {np.median(train_orders):,.0f} now: {np.median(this_week):,.0f}") print(f"KS statistic = {stat:.3f}, p-value = {p:.2e}") print("ALERT: drift detected" if p < 0.01 else "no significant drift") OUTPUT median then: 1,856 now: 2,401 KS statistic = 0.211, p-value = 2.25e-27 ALERT: drift detected What to monitor Example signal Service health Error rate, response time, uptime Input data Missing values, new categories, shifted distributions Predictions Share of "fraud" predictions suddenly doubles RAG systems Refusal rate, citation clicks, user thumbs up and down ✦ KEY IDEA Decide in advance what will trigger retraining, such as a drift alert or accuracy below a set level, so a

new categories, shifted distributions Predictions Share of "fraud" predictions suddenly doubles RAG systems Refusal rate, citation clicks, user thumbs up and down ✦ KEY IDEA Decide in advance what will trigger retraining, such as a drift alert or accuracy below a set level, so a slow decline never goes unnoticed.

8.6 Responsible and secure AI A model that is accurate on average can still be unfair to a group, leak private data, or be tricked by a malicious input. Responsible deployment plans for all three. Risk Example Practice Bias A loan model is less accurate for one region Measure metrics per group, not only overall Privacy Logs store customers' phone numbers Collect only what you need; mask personal data Prompt injection An uploaded PDF says "ignore your rules" Treat documents as data; limit what the model can do Abuse and cost A script sends thousands of requests Rate limits, size limits, quotas Over-trust Users accept answers without checking Show sources, confidence and refusals ◆REA L- WORLDCASESTUDY Checking a model by group The 2018 Gender Shades study by Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru found that commercial face-analysis systems were far less accurate on darker-skinned women than on lighter-skinned men, although overall accuracy looked high. Several vendors improved their systems after the results were published. Breaking metrics down by group is now a standard step before launch. ✓ Launch checklist: versioned model, automated tests, secrets in environment variables, input validation, rate limits, per-group metrics, monitoring with alerts, and a rollback plan. ✦ KEY IDEA Trust is a feature. Clear sources, honest refusals and protected data make people willing to rely on an AI product.

9.2 The indexing pipeline Indexing turns uploaded PDFs into searchable chunks. It runs once per document, right after upload. 1 Extract. PDF.js reads each page’s text in the browser, along with its printed page label (section 7.2). 2 Clean. Collapse whitespace, re-join hyphenated words, and drop lines that repeat on every page, such as running headers. 3 Chunk. Split each page separately into about 300 tokens with about 60 tokens of overlap, prefixed with the file name. 4 Embed. Send chunk texts in batches to /api/embed , which returns one normalised vector per chunk. 5 Store. Keep vectors and metadata in browser memory, ready for search. Nothing is written to the server. Python · index_page.py import re def chunk_page(file, label, text, size=60, overlap=12): words = re.sub(r"-\s+(\w)", r"\1", text).split() # fix "exam- ple" step = size - overlap return [{"file": file, "page": label, "text": " ".join(words[i:i + size])} for i in range(0, max(len(words) - overlap, 1), step)] page_text = "Overlap repeats a few sentences between neighbouring chunks. "*9 chunks = chunk_page("Neural_Ink.pdf", "51", page_text) print(len(page_text.split()), "words _>", len(chunks), "chunks") print(chunks[1]["file"], "page", chunks[1]["page"], "|", chunks[1]["text"][:48]) OUTPUT 72 words _> 2 chunks Neural_Ink.pdf page 51 | Overlap repeats a few sentences between neighbou Real chunks are measured in tokens; counting words, as here, is a close and simple approximation (about 3 words for every 4 tokens in English).

9.3 The query pipeline For every question, Citelle searches, decides whether to answer, and then writes a cited answer. Python · query_pipeline.py import numpy as np def search(q_vec, chunk_vecs, k=5): scores = chunk_vecs @ q_vec # vectors are normalised top = np.argsort(scores)[_:-1][:k] return [(int(i), float(scores[i])) for i in top] def answer_or_refuse(hits, threshold=0.35): if not hits or hits[0][1] < threshold: return {"refused": True, "message": "I couldn't find this in your documents."} return {"refused": False, "use_chunks": [i for i, s in hits if s _= threshold]} rng = np.random.default_rng(3) vecs = rng.normal(size=(200, 384)); vecs _= np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1)[:, None] on_topic = vecs[42] + rng.normal(scale=0.03, size=384) off_topic = rng.normal(size=384) for name, q in [("on topic", on_topic), ("off topic", off_topic)]: q=q/ np.linalg.norm(q) print(name, "_>", answer_or_refuse(search(q, vecs))) OUTPUT on topic _> {'refused': False, 'use_chunks': [42]} off topic _> {'refused': True, 'message': "I couldn't find this in your documents."} When the threshold is passed, the selected chunks are numbered and sent to /api/answer with the grounded prompt from section 7.6. The answer streams back word by word, and each [n] marker in it becomes a clickable chip showing the file and page. Setting Value Why Top-k 5 Enough context without diluting the prompt Threshold Tuned per model Set from a test set of answerable and unanswerable questions Temperature 0.2 Factual, repeatable answers

9.4 Keeping it safe and reliable A public demo meets real users, slow networks and occasional abuse. A few defensive habits keep it fast, private and online. Risk Defence in Citelle Leaked API key The key lives only in the hosting platform’s environment variables Huge uploads Limits on file size, page count and number of files Request floods Size limits on every endpoint and a cap on chunks per request Prompt injection Sources are wrapped and labelled as reference data, never instructions Invented citations Citation numbers are checked against the chunks actually sent Model outage or quota Automatic fallback to another model, then to keyword search with quoted passages Graceful degradation If the AI service is unavailable, Citelle still works. It switches to keyword search (BM25, section 7.5) and shows the best matching passages as direct quotes, each with its file and page. The interface says clearly which mode is active, so users are never misled about how an answer was produced. ▲ PRIVACY BY DESIGN Uploaded PDFs are never stored on the server. Only the text of the chunks needed for a question is sent to the AI model, and only for that request. Closing the browser tab clears the library. ✦ KEY IDEA Design for failure from day one.
